semantic_changes: The transfer is issued concurrently with the demotion instead of after it converges.
Each attempt uses a fresh cluster, which is required because the demotion changes the configuration permanently.
The result is summarised across 20 attempts rather than reported per case, and includes how many attempts ended with the target as a non-voter.

scope.description: Twenty independent attempts, each on a fresh four-voter in-memory cluster. Per attempt the harness picks the leader and one follower, starts DemoteVoter for that follower on a goroutine, then immediately calls LeadershipTransferToServer for the same member on whichever node is leader at that moment, both with bounded waits. It records whether each future succeeded, whether the target ever reported Leader during the following two seconds, which member led at the end, and the target's own suffrage at the end.
assumptions: Starting the demotion and issuing the transfer without an intervening wait is the tightest race the public API allows; the caller cannot observe commit state between the two calls without waiting.
The target is chosen at demotion time from the members that are not leading, so the demotion never targets the sitting leader.
An attempt in which the target reports Leader at any sample counts as an elevation even if it later steps down.
excluded: No repeated demotions on one cluster; a fresh cluster is built per attempt because a member can be demoted only once.
No partition, no restart, and no client traffic during the race.
The transfer target's address is read before the demotion, so a member whose address changed as part of the demotion is out of scope.

basis.prefix: The harness bootstraps a four-voter cluster through the cluster helper, reads the leader and the first non-leader member, records the target's identifier and address, starts DemoteVoter(target, 5s) on a goroutine, re-reads the leader, and immediately starts LeadershipTransferToServer(target, address) on a goroutine as well. It waits up to five seconds for the demotion future and up to three for the transfer future, recording both results. It then samples the target's State every 10 ms for two seconds, recording whether the target ever reports Leader, reads the cluster's leader at the end, and reads the target's own configuration to record its final suffrage. After all attempts it emits cv_result_demotion_race with the attempt count, how many demotions succeeded, how many transfers succeeded, how many attempts saw the target lead, how many ended with the target leading, how many ended with the target as a non-voter, and the last transfer error.
basis.responsibility: A transfer must not install a member as leader while the configuration that removes its vote is in flight. The public API offers no way to make the demotion and the transfer atomic, so the question is whether the ordering the library itself imposes, with voters rejecting a candidate their applied configuration no longer counts, is enough to prevent the elevation when the two requests are issued back to back.

comparisons.description: A member whose vote is being removed must not become leader in any attempt, even when the transfer races the demotion.
No attempt may end with the demoted member leading.
All twenty transfer futures are expected to complete without error, which is what makes the absence of elevation a silent failure rather than a reported one.
